main/sysdolphin/baselib/rumble:HSD_Rumbl.value: Sets the rumble subsystem's global suppression flag, allowing all four controller motors and all scheduled rumble processing to be suspended or resumed without discarding the queued rumble programs.
main/sysdolphin/baselib/rumble:HSD_Rumbl.rationale: The target atomically writes the shared RumbleInfo flag. HSD_PadRumbleInterpret tests that flag before consulting any channel's direct state or interpreting its request list; when the flag is set, every channel remains at status zero, while clearing it allows the preserved direct and queued state to be processed again.

evidence.why: Shows the target writing the shared flag and the four-channel interpreter using that flag to suppress direct rumble, queued-command advancement, and nonzero motor output.

main/sysdolphin/baselib/rumble:HSD_Rumbl.value: The flag transition is atomic with respect to interrupt-driven rumble work: the routine saves and disables the current interrupt state, writes the global flag, and restores the saved state. While the stored flag is nonzero, each interpretation pass forces every channel toward motor status zero and freezes queued programs because their command cursors, waits, frame lifetimes, and loop counters are not advanced. Clearing the flag resumes processing from the preserved program state.
main/sysdolphin/baselib/rumble:HSD_Rumbl.rationale: The current implementation still protects only the shared-flag write and bypasses direct-state seeding and request interpretation while the flag is nonzero. The refreshed request layout confirms which execution fields remain untouched during that bypass, and the output stage still dispatches a resulting transition to zero when necessary.

evidence.why: Defines the request command cursor, wait, frame lifetime, loop state, status, and pause fields preserved while interpretation is bypassed.
Shows the interrupt-protected flag write and the nonzero flag bypassing direct and scheduled interpretation while channel status remains zero.
Shows a resulting transition to zero being dispatched to the corresponding controller motor and cached as the previous state.

src/sysdolphin/baselib/rumble.c.value: Gameplay-facing routines create and mutate HSD_PadRumbleListData records drawn from HSD_PadLibData.rumble_info and attach them to one of four HSD_RumbleData records. HSD_PadRumbleInterpret advances each unpaused command list, combines its resulting status with the channel's direct status, removes completed records, and calls PADControlMotor only when the computed motor status differs from the channel's previous status.

src/sysdolphin/baselib/rumble.c.value: Each controller channel maintains direct, current, and previous motor states plus a priority-ordered list of timed sequences. Sequence interpretation is suspended while a record's pause flag is set; otherwise commands can select stop, off, or on states, establish and repeat loops, decrement waits and finite lifetimes, and remove a sequence when it terminates. Hardware is updated only on a computed state transition.
src/sysdolphin/baselib/rumble.c.rationale: The current header retains all channel and request execution fields, while the interpreter preserves the pause guard, encoded status transitions, loop and timer updates, completion handling, and changed-state-only hardware dispatch.
